implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design outputs and dissemination
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products and services to be produced, including the related systems, tools and procedures used in the Disseminate phase. Processes governing access to any confidential outputs are also designed here. Outputs should be designed to follow existing standards wherever possible, so inputs to this process may include metadata from similar or previous collections (including extractions from statistical, administrative, geospatial and other non-statistical registers and databases), international standards, and information about practices in other statistical organisations from sub-process 1.1 (Identify needs). Outputs may also be designed in partnership with other interested bodies, particularly if they are considered to be joint outputs, or they will be disseminated by another organisation.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products, and services to be produced, including all systems, tools, and procedures to be used in dissemination. Automated and AI-supported solutions are used wherever possible to produce initial output templates, align with existing standards, generate metadata, and configure dissemination tools, allowing staff to focus on innovative features and context-specific requirements, including confidentiality. All outputs and dissemination artifacts must be standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable, with support for APIs, comprehensive metadata tagging, and open formats to maximize interoperability, discoverability, and reusability by human and machine clients. The process includes an explicit, early review of the type and necessity of products, especially visualizations, with the expectation that only those genuinely required for user value or compliance are designed—allowing exclusion where end-users can self-serve or alternatives suffice. Outputs may also be designed in partnership with external organizations, ensuring full alignment with digital-to-digital workflows and standards.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' is implicated because they 'edit, validate, market, and disseminate data,' 'review and assess data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' and 'interpret client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations.' As output and dissemination design is automated and standardized, this officer will focus on QA, metadata validation, and supporting fit-for-purpose output design—including selection/omission of visualization types—ensuring robust machine-actionability and user-centered dissemination.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Reuse or build dissemination components
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new components or reuse existing components needed for the dissemination of statistical products as designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination). All types of dissemination components are included, from those that produce traditional paper publications to those that provide web services, (linked) open data outputs, geospatial statistics, maps, or access to microdata.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new or reuse existing automation-ready dissemination components needed for the release of statistical products as designated in sub-process 2.1. Dissemination modules—spanning web services, open data, geospatial outputs, microdata access, and even traditional products—are built or upgraded for modularity, machine-actionability, and AI/automation-enabled production. Dynamic output generation, versioning, metadata enrichment, and seamless integration with downstream APIs are all standard, with automation ensuring real-time release, update, and consistency of all published outputs. Human staff are responsible for policy oversight, exception handling, and refinement of complex or user-specific dissemination features that automation cannot yet address.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The GSBPM update implies dissemination modules must be 'modular, API-enabled, and designed to support automated production and update of data tables, microsites, APIs, and open data endpoints.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' role includes 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'reviews and assesses data quality,' and 'participates on data production and dissemination teams.' Their job is now more focused on automation-based, QA-centric, and technical oversight of dissemination component builds and upgrades, ensuring standards, interoperability, automation compatibility, and effectiveness of delivery channels.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Prepare draft outputs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process is where the data from sub-processes 5.7 (Calculate aggregates) and 5.8 (Finalise data files) are transformed into statistical outputs, which could include indexes, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, microdata, etc. The preparation of maps, GIS outputs and geo-statistical services can be included to maximise the value and capacity to analyse the statistical information. Methodological notes, to accompany the outputs and describe how they have been produced are also prepared in this sub-process taking as input the methodology designed in the Design phase. When new processing or analysis methods such as those based on machine learning or artificial intelligence are used, additional explanations might need to be prepared to communicate/explain the necessary information to the users.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process transforms processed and finalized data into statistical outputs using automated, AI-powered pipelines. Outputs—including indices, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, geo-statistical services, write-ups, dashboards, and methodological documentation—are generated by default through LLM/AI-driven automation. Human analysts intervene to interpret, refine, or tailor outputs for specialized, complex, or critical communication needs. AI-generated methodological notes and narratives accompany all outputs, documenting analytic approaches and logic. This automation-first approach maximizes efficiency, consistency, and allows analysts to focus on providing added value and insight.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' ('edits, validates, markets and disseminates data', 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used') will increasingly focus on editing and validating automatically-produced analytical and narrative products, ensuring that AI-generated content is accessible, accurate, and suitable for intended audiences.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Validate outputs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process is where statisticians validate the outputs produced, in accordance with a general quality framework and with expectations and also comparing with auxiliary information available (e.g. from previous cycles or from other sources). This sub-process may include activities involved with the gathering of intelligence, with the cumulative effect of building up a body of knowledge about a specific statistical domain, in order to check for errors and validate the data as objectively as possible. This knowledge is then applied to the current collection, in the current environment, to identify any divergence from expectations and to allow informed analyses. Validation activities can include: Comparing the statistics with previous cycles (if applicable); Checking that the associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators are present and in line with expectations; Checking geospatial consistency of the data; Confronting the statistics against other relevant data (both internal and external); Investigating inconsistencies in the statistics; Performing macro editing; Checking aggregates as a validation for a microdata set; Validating the statistics against expectations and domain intelligence.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process is where outputs are validated using automated, AI- and ML-powered, real-time digital workflows. Anomaly detection, benchmarking against historical data, metadata and paradata checks, macro editing, and internal/external confrontations are executed with machine-driven QA and pattern recognition. Complex, novel, or ambiguous findings are escalated to human statistics experts for review and contextual analysis, ensuring that outputs are validated rapidly, consistently, and with high assurance of quality.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer', who 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' will be responsible for interpreting and confirming automated QA outcomes, updating validation protocols, and supporting the refinement of machine-driven validation pipelines.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Apply disclosure control
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process ensures that the data (and metadata) to be disseminated or internally stored for future use do not breach the appropriate rules on confidentiality according to either organisational policies and rules, or to the process-specific methodology created in sub-process 2.5 (Design processing and analysis). This may include checks for primary and secondary disclosure, as well as the application of data suppression or perturbation techniques and output checking. The degree and method of statistical disclosure control may vary for different types of outputs. For example, the approach used for microdata sets for research purposes will be different to that for published tables or visualisations at the aggregated level. Geospatial data or outputs from geospatial data may raise additional confidentiality challenges in terms of personal data protection and disclosure risk.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process applies disclosure control by default using AI-driven, automation-enabled privacy/SCD tools, which automatically assess, suppress, or perturb outputs for confidentiality per established policy. All actions are digitally logged and audited. Outputs only reach human reviewers when the automation detects elevated, ambiguous, or non-standard disclosure risks, ensuring privacy compliance by default and at scale.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Disclosure control is now performed by 'AI-driven, automation-enabled privacy/SCD tools,' with staff reviewing 'elevated, ambiguous, or non-standard disclosure risks.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer', who is involved in 'editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical data' and is 'responsible for the application of data suppression or perturbation techniques and output checking,' will become the principal authority in reviewing flagged disclosure risks, confirming privacy decisions escalated by AI, and documenting disclosure rationale and actions.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Finalise outputs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process ensures the statistics and associated information are fit for purpose and reach the required quality level and are thus ready for use. It includes: Completing consistency checks; Determining the level of release, and applying caveats; Collating supporting information, including interpretation, commentary, technical notes, briefings, measures of uncertainty and any other necessary metadata; Producing the supporting internal documents; Conducting pre-release discussion with appropriate internal subject matter experts; Translating the statistical outputs in countries with multilingual dissemination; Approving the statistical content for release.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process finalises and packages outputs using digital, automation-driven tools and workflows, ensuring all required metadata, commentary, technical notes, consistency checks, and documentation are produced and collated automatically to the highest standard. Human experts are responsible for sign-off, review of flagged anomalies, and decision-making on exceptional release scenarios or nuanced dissemination requirements. Routine approval, translation, and pre-release briefing are streamlined by digital platforms, maximizing output quality and deployment speed.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: GSBPM requires 'automation for all routine checks, collation, evidence-gathering, and documentation for dissemination,' reserving human involvement for quality assurance and complex scenarios. The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer,' with expertise in 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' and 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output… analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' will verify automated output packages, complete QA review, approve for release, and handle nuanced or exceptional dissemination scenarios.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Disseminate
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase manages the release of the statistical data and their products to users. It includes all activities associated with assembling and releasing a range of static and dynamic products via a range of channels. These activities support users to access and use the products released by the statistical organisation. For statistical products produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. Cataloguing and tagging released data and products using relevant metadata standards can greatly increase their discoverability and accessibility both internally and externally. International standards should be used as a norm to ensure that they can be found and consumed easily across a broad range of users. Linking data to geospatial classifications in particular can allow for detailed geographical presentation of outputs. While GSBPM conceives of archiving as taking place within the overarching Data Management and Metadata Management activities, its relevance to finalised outputs in this phase should be noted. The Disseminate phase is broken down into five sub-processes (Figure 13), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase manages the release of statistical data and their products to users using automation-driven, API-first, and metadata-enriched delivery workflows and platforms. All assembling, cataloguing, metadata enrichment, and release processes are automated and performed in real-time, producing products that are dynamically accessible, searchable, and machine-actionable by both human and AI agents. Outputs are prepared for API-driven consumption, optimized for AI search, and enriched with comprehensive metadata to ensure discovery and reuse across systems. Human staff engage only for policy setting, exception handling, and specialized user support. The Disseminate phase is structured into five sub-processes (Figure 13), which may operate sequentially, in parallel, or iteratively, as best fits the digital dissemination ecosystem.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: GSBPM now mandates full automation and digitization for dissemination—'all assembling, cataloguing, metadata enrichment, and release processes are automated and performed in real-time, producing products that are dynamically accessible, searchable, and machine-actionable.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer', who 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data', and 'participates on data production and dissemination teams', is now focused on overseeing these automated data release platforms, advising on metadata enrichment, troubleshooting exceptions, and supporting users in digital-first dissemination environments.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Update output systems
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process manages the update of systems (e.g. databases) where data and metadata are stored ready for dissemination purposes, including: Formatting data and metadata ready to be put into output systems; Loading data and metadata into output systems; Ensuring data are linked to the relevant metadata. Formatting, loading and linking of metadata should preferably mostly take place in earlier phases, but this sub-process includes a final check that all of the necessary metadata are in place ready for dissemination.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process manages the update of output systems and databases for dissemination using automated, real-time loading of data and enriched metadata. Machine-actionable formatting, digital linkage, and metadata validation are built-in, ensuring that all disseminated products are AI- and API-consumable, searchable, and enriched with discoverability standards. Final checks for completeness and metadata enrichment are automatic, and all outputs are designed for seamless use by both human and digital consumers.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The GSBPM update requires output systems to be 'auto-loading, metadata-enriched, machine-actionable outputs, ready for API-driven digital release.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' ('provides statistical data and consultative services to users', 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata') will supervise the metadata enrichment, ensure linkages are complete for discoverability, and validate the technical correctness of machine-actionable outputs before release.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Produce dissemination products
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process produces the dissemination products, as previously designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination), to meet user needs. They could include publications, press releases and websites. The products can take many forms including interactive graphics, tables, maps, public-use microdata sets, linked open data and downloadable files. When the final products raise concern for confidentiality, additional disclosure control may be considered and applied via sub-process 6.4 (Apply disclosure control). Typical steps include: Preparing the product components (explanatory texts, tables, charts, maps, quality statements etc.); Assembling the components into products; Editing the products and checking that they meet publication standards.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process produces dissemination outputs using automated, AI- and LLM-powered workflows to generate, assemble, and format all products—including publications, press releases, online tables, interactive graphics, maps, and PUMFs—as standard. Text, graphics, and narrative products are created with digital automation as first resort, and all products (including mandatory PUMFs) are checked for standards adherence by human specialists, who refine outputs and ensure audience appropriateness as required. All dissemination outputs are machine-actionable, metadata-enriched, and ready for instant digital release.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Production must be 'automated and AI-driven,' with LLMs drafting all textual and visualization products for human review and refinement. The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' ('edits, validates... disseminates data', 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output') becomes a key reviewer, validator, and adapter of AI-created reports, tables, summaries, graphics, and—when required—Public Use Microdata Files (PUMFs).

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Release dissemination products
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process ensures that all elements for the release are in place including managing the timing of the release. It includes briefings for specific groups such as the press or ministers, as well as the arrangements for any pre-release embargoes. It also includes the provision of products to subscribers, and managing access to confidential data by authorised user groups, such as researchers. Sometimes an organisation may need to retract a product, for example, if an error is discovered. This is also included in this sub-process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process releases dissemination products using digital automation to handle all elements of release—timing, briefing, embargo, subscriber access, and confidential data management. Orchestration platforms schedule, log, and manage real-time releases. Human staff review and approve exception cases, interact with high-level subscribers, and handle policy or retraction scenarios as required, ensuring transparency and compliance at all times.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Release, timing, access and embargo management are handled via 'orchestrated, automated, and logged digital systems.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' ('participates on data production and dissemination teams,' 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users') will focus on exception review, approval of high-profile or embargoed releases, and liaison with key clients such as researchers.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Promote dissemination products
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: Whilst marketing in general can be considered to be part of GAMSO, this sub-process concerns the active promotion of the statistical products produced in a specific statistical business process, to help them reach the widest possible audience. It includes the use of customer relationship management tools, to better target potential users of the products, as well as the use of tools including websites and other platforms like social media to facilitate the process of communicating statistical information to users. These activities may be coordinated with partners in the case of joint products.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process promotes statistical products using AI/automation-driven tools to generate, recommend, and deploy messaging across all platforms—web, email, social, and beyond. Content, format, and strategy are tailored with AI for each target audience, adjusting to maximize reach and impact. Staff intervene for high-level campaign review, optimization, and the management of complex or sensitive outreach.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Promotion is now 'automated and AI-driven, with messaging, format, and channel recommendations adjusted in real time.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' (whose duties include 'markets and disseminates data,' and 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data') must review, validate, and optimize AI-prompted outreach messages and campaigns, and is responsible for quality assurance of critical communications across platforms.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Provide user support
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process ensures that user queries and requests for services such as microdata access are recorded, and that responses are provided within agreed deadlines. These queries and requests should be regularly reviewed to provide an input to the overarching Quality Management activity, as they can indicate new or changing user needs. Replies to user requests can also be used to populate a knowledge database or a “Frequently Asked Questions” page, that is made publicly available, thus reducing the burden of replying to repeated and/or similar requests from external users. This sub-process also includes managing support to any partner organisations involved in disseminating the products.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process provides user support through AI-powered chatbots and automation interfaces, which record, triage, and answer user queries in real time, guiding users to datasets, data interpretations, and publications as needed. Complex inquiries and escalations go to human staff for resolution, especially for nuanced, sensitive, or high-value support. User feedback and request tracking are used to populate knowledge bases and feed into service quality improvement.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: GSBPM requires 'user support through AI-powered chatbots and automation interfaces.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' (responsible for 'providing statistical data and consultative services to users') will be escalated complex or high-priority queries, oversee knowledgebase curation, and provide input on improving AI/automated FAQ and support workflows.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Specify needs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options and preparing a business case, which may weigh the benefits of addressing these needs against expected costs, risks and other requirements, considering the public good arising from meeting those needs and the implications for respondents, users and other stakeholders. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options, and preparing a business case. In the modernized statistical environment, these activities are increasingly supported by automated and AI-powered processes—ranging from the synthesis and structuring of stakeholder inputs, through the analysis of options, to the automated drafting of business case materials. Routine and repetitive aspects of needs identification, consultation, and documentation are minimized for manual intervention, enabling staff to focus on higher-value tasks: interpreting context, establishing priorities, and making strategic decisions that cannot be automated. The phase thus leverages end-to-end process automation and AI wherever possible, supporting greater efficiency, responsiveness, and quality at the earliest stage of the statistical business process. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' participates in 'the analysis of statistical program data,' 'suggests possible feedback on collection... and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' As needs investigation becomes automated, this role adapts from manual environmental scanning to 'assessing the validity of collected and processed data,' now largely in partnership with AI and automated feedback synthesis. Their responsibilities for analyzing feedback, preparing recommendations, and interpreting user needs are now less about manual collation and more about oversight, validation, and nuanced contextualization of AI findings. Their knowledge of data flows and evaluation techniques will be directed toward managing and supervising AI-driven inputs and focusing effort on the highest value-add problems.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Identify needs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics. It may be triggered by a new information request from users, an environmental change such as a reduced budget, a periodic review, or respondent feedback. Action plans from evaluations of previous iterations of the production cycle (including from respondent feedback) or from other programmes might provide an input to this sub-process. It also includes consideration of practice amongst other (national and international) statistical organisations producing similar data and the methods used by those organisations.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics. In the modern process, AI and automated tools are used to continuously scan for new information requests from users, detect relevant environmental changes, and aggregate respondent feedback and evaluation action plans. These technologies also benchmark needs by automatically referencing practices among other (national and international) statistical organizations. Automation supports the collation, analysis, and structuring of these triggers for new or changed statistics, while staff focus their expertise on interpreting context, confirming significance, and ensuring response to complex or emergent requirements.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' participates in 'the analysis of statistical program data,' 'suggests possible feedback on collection... and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' As needs investigation becomes automated, this role adapts from manual environmental scanning to 'assessing the validity of collected and processed data,' now largely in partnership with AI and automated feedback synthesis.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Consult and confirm needs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process focuses on consulting with the internal and external stakeholders and confirming in detail the needs for the statistics. A good understanding of user needs is required so that the statistical organisation knows not only what it is expected to deliver, but also when, how, and perhaps most importantly, why. For the second and subsequent iterations of this sub-process, the main focus will be on determining whether previously identified needs have changed. This detailed understanding of user needs is the critical part of this sub-process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process focuses on consulting with internal and external stakeholders and confirming in detail the needs for the statistics. Automated and AI-supported systems are now used to organize and analyze input from stakeholders, including feedback, evolving requirements, and historical engagement. These tools facilitate discovery of patterns and highlight changes in user needs over time. Statistical staff engage directly where nuanced negotiation, detailed interpretation, or complex prioritization is required, ensuring that automated summaries and analytics are supplemented by expert, context-aware judgment. This detailed understanding of user needs and the efficient, technology-enabled consultation process are both critical to this sub-process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' 'provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.' In the context of automated feedback organization, this becomes a quality and prioritization oversight role for stakeholder requirements, rather than a manual aggregator. The work-description's emphasis on 'liaising with subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate requirements' aligns with consulting and confirming needs with AI assistance.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Establish output objectives
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process identifies the statistical output objectives that are required to meet the user needs confirmed in sub-process 1.2 (Consult and confirm needs). It includes agreeing the suitability of the proposed outputs and their quality measures with users. Legal or normative frameworks (e.g. relating to confidentiality, methodologies), and available resources are important to consider when establishing output objectives.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process identifies the statistical output objectives that are required to meet the user needs confirmed in sub-process 1.2 (Consult and confirm needs). AI and automated tools aggregate and analyze confirmed user requirements, historical deliverables, legal/normative frameworks, and available resource constraints to generate draft output objectives and candidate quality measures. Staff provide oversight by aligning these drafts with strategic intent, adjudicating complex trade-offs, and ensuring compliance with legal and methodological expectations. This shift supports more efficient, responsive, and high-quality output objective-setting by leveraging technology for foundational work and human expertise for final judgment and alignment.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' role of providing 'analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations' is directly relevant. Their focus shifts to confirming appropriateness of AI-proposed output objectives, ensuring compliance with standards and legal requirements.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Identify concepts
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process clarifies the required concepts to be measured from the point of view of the users. At this stage, the concepts identified might not align with existing statistical standards. This alignment, and the choice or definition of the statistical and other concepts and variables to be used, takes place in sub-process 2.2 (Design variables).
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process clarifies the required concepts to be measured from the point of view of the users. Automated and AI-assisted tools are leveraged to synthesize user requirements, prior documentation, and relevant internal/external sources, providing preliminary suggestions and structured options for possible concepts. The role of the subject matter sponsor is central—this person or group is solely accountable for the final specification and formal certification of the required concepts prior to downstream design or standard alignment. This approach minimizes manual tasks, maintains clear accountability, and increases speed and efficiency in the establishment of robust conceptual frameworks.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The update highlights two changes: (1) AI/automation supports 'synthesize user requirements, prior documentation, and relevant internal/external sources,' and (2) the 'subject matter sponsor is solely accountable' for final specification and certification. The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' must now validate AI-suggested concepts and is accountable for final specification, as the work-description specifies knowledge of 'statistical or economic theory and principles... and methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation...' and liaising to 'develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development.' Their responsibilities now heavily involve overseeing AI-supported proposals, certifying their validity, and documenting concept definition for downstream design.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Check data availability and suitability
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use. An assessment of possible alternatives would normally include research into potential administrative or other non-statistical sources of data (e.g. privately-held data or “Big Data”), to: Determine whether they would be suitable for use for statistical purposes (e.g. the extent to which administrative concepts match data requirements, and whether the timeliness and quality of the data, security, and continuity of data supply are suitable); Assess the division of responsibilities between data suppliers and the statistical organisation; Check necessary ICT resources (e.g. data storage, technology required to handle incoming data and data processing) as well as any provision agreements with data suppliers (which could be legal or other agreements such as memoranda of understanding) for accessing and sharing the data (e.g. formats, delivery, accompanying metadata and quality check). When existing sources have been assessed, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps in the data requirement is prepared. This may include identifying possible partnerships with data holders or conducting a new survey to collect data if necessary. This sub-process also includes a more general assessment of the legal framework in which data would be collected and used, and may therefore identify proposals for changes to existing legislation or the introduction of a new legal framework.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process systematically checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use. Existing data holdings must be exhaustively investigated and prioritized first, followed by a search for relevant administrative and alternative data sources; the option to conduct new surveys is only considered if these avenues prove insufficient to meet data needs. The subject matter sponsor holds sole accountability for certifying that all relevant avenues for data have been thoroughly explored and that the suitability, timeliness, and quality of any proposed source have been rigorously assessed. To expedite and strengthen the acquisition of administrative and alternative data, a center of expertise works collaboratively with subject matter specialists to support negotiations, acquisition logistics, and the establishment of legal or operational agreements where needed. When multiple avenues have been assessed and documented, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps is prepared. This sub-process also encompasses the assessment and possible updates to the legal framework for data collection, ensuring fit-for-purpose, respondent-efficient, and timely data acquisition and usage.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: With the update, the process must now 'formalize a strict hierarchy of data sourcing—first considering existing data holdings, then administrative and alternative data, and only lastly, new survey data collection.' Further, the 'subject matter sponsor holds sole accountability,' and a 'center of expertise works collaboratively.' The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' is deeply implicated, as their work-description emphasizes assessing the 'validity of collected and processed data,' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' They must now systematically evaluate automated outputs about available data sources, certify the thoroughness and suitability, and partner with the designated data acquisition teams.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Prepare and submit business case
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process documents the findings of the other sub-processes in this phase, in the form of a business case to get approval to implement the new or modified statistical business process. Such a business case would need to conform to the requirements of the approval body, but would typically include elements such as: A description of the “As-Is” business process (if it already exists), with information on how the current statistics are produced, highlighting any inefficiencies and issues to be addressed; The proposed “To-Be” solution, detailing how the statistical business process will be developed to produce the new or revised statistics; An assessment of costs and benefits against objectives and any external constraints. The business case describes options and makes recommendations. It may include the benefits, costs, deliverables, time frame, budget, required technical and human resources, risk assessment and impact on stakeholders for each option. After the business case is prepared, it is submitted for approval to move to the next phase of the business process. At this sub-process, a “go”/“no go” decision is made. Typically, the business case is reviewed and formally approved or disapproved by the appropriate sponsors and governance committees.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Validate outputs

This sub-process may include activities involved with the gathering of intelligence, with the cumulative effect of building up a body of knowledge about a specific statistical domain, in order to check for errors and validate the data as objectively as possible. This knowledge is then applied to the current collection, in the current environment, to identify any divergence from expectations and to allow informed analyses. Validation activities can include: Comparing the statistics with previous cycles (if applicable); Checking that the associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators are present and in line with expectations; Checking geospatial consistency of the data; Confronting the statistics against other relevant data (both internal and external); Investigating inconsistencies in the statistics; Performing macro editing; Checking aggregates as a validation for a microdata set; Validating the statistics against expectations and domain intelligence.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Check data availability and suitability

When existing sources have been assessed, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps in the data requirement is prepared. This may include identifying possible partnerships with data holders or conducting a new survey to collect data if necessary. This sub-process also includes a more general assessment of the legal framework in which data would be collected and used, and may therefore identify proposals for changes to existing legislation or the introduction of a new legal framework.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Design collection
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process prepares a collection strategy for the data, and determines the most appropriate collection instruments and methods, which may depend on the type of data collection, the collection unit type (enterprise, person, or other) and the available sources of data. The actual activities in this sub-process will vary according to the type of collection instrument required, which can include computer assisted interviewing, paper questionnaires, administrative registers, automated and semi-automated data transfer methods (such as using APIs, machine-to-machine integrations and various types of file transfers), web-scraping technologies as well as technology for geospatial data. The collection may employ a multi-mode method which requires additional considerations such as design of sequencing or different instruments for different modes. Direct or indirect use of administrative data may be introduced in the data collection mode for either controlling survey data or assisting it when capturing survey information. In the case of survey (or census) data, this collection strategy includes the design of the collection instruments, questions and response templates (in conjunction with the variables and statistical classifications designed in sub-process 2.2 (Design variables)). This sub-process may include design of fieldwork operations, and respondent engagement, in the case of survey data collection. It also includes the confirmation of existing agreements or creation of new agreements. This sub-process is enabled by tools such as question libraries (to facilitate the reuse of questions and related attributes), questionnaire tools (to enable the quick and easy compilation of questions into formats suitable for cognitive testing) and agreement templates (to help standardise terms and conditions). This sub-process also includes the design of respondent management systems that are specific to this business process. Common sources for a sampling frame are administrative and statistical registers, censuses and information from other sample surveys. It may refer to geospatial data and classifications. This sub-process describes how these sources can be combined if needed. Analysis of whether the frame covers the target population should be performed. Spatial analysis techniques can be used to ensure the spatial distribution of the units is appropriate. A sampling plan should be made. The actual sample is created in sub-process 4.1 (Create frame and select sample), using the methodology specified in this sub-process.

The GSBPM can be used to design a statistical organisation’s business architecture layer when a statistical organisation has an existing enterprise architecture in place. The design might be adjusted to fit the organisation. A general principle is to reuse processes and technology across many statistical business processes, so existing production solutions (e.g. services, systems and databases) should be examined first, to determine whether they are fit for purpose for this specific production process, then, if any gaps are identified, new solutions can be designed. This sub-process also considers how staff will interact with systems and who will be responsible for what and when.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process determines the workflow from data collection to dissemination, ensuring all production processes are seamlessly integrated, modular, and event-driven, with automation and AI/ML supporting orchestration, monitoring, and transitions. Workflows are designed to minimize manual intervention and maximize real-time coordination, leveraging digital platforms and automation for every routine or standardized task. The emphasis is on building touchless, continuous data pipelines that allow for automated validation, routing, escalation, and exception reporting. Existing automated solutions and system components are reused wherever possible; if new components are needed, they are built automation- and integration-ready from inception. Staff responsibilities focus on system oversight, addressing exceptions and inefficiencies, and iteratively improving and upgrading automated workflows for future resilience and scalability.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is expected to support and validate 'modular, automation-ready, and event-driven digital pipelines,' ensuring end-to-end system integrity and smooth transitions between all process phases. Their technical skills, knowledge of workflow configuration, and partnership on 'project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis' will now be directed toward the implementation and refinement of digital-first, inter-operable workflows across the statistic production lifecycle.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Build
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase builds and tests the production solution to the point where it is ready for use in the 'live' environment. The outputs of the Design phase are assembled and configured in this phase to create the complete operational environment to run the process. New services are built by exception, created in response to gaps in the existing catalogue of services sourced from within the organisation and externally. These new services are constructed to be broadly reusable in alignment with the business architecture of the organisation where possible, and compliant with security requirements. For statistical outputs produced on a regular basis, this phase usually occurs for the first iteration, following a review or a change in methodology or technology, rather than for every iteration. The Build phase is broken down into seven sub-processes (Figure 9), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative. Some approaches used to develop tools and systems involve iteration between sub-processes in the Design and Build phases. The first three sub-processes are concerned with the development and improvement of systems used in collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of data. The last four subprocesses focus on the end-to-end process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase builds and tests the production solution to the point where it is ready for use in the 'live' environment, leveraging modular automation and AI-driven assembly at every step. The outputs of the Design phase are assembled and configured using digital orchestration pipelines that prioritize reusability, traceability, and compliance with business architecture and security requirements. Automated configuration, integration, and self-testing are employed wherever possible, enabling rapid, reliable, and consistent system deployment. Human expertise is reserved for overseeing automated processes, handling exceptions that cannot be resolved by automation, and driving continuous improvement in modular service creation. New services are developed only to fill gaps, and are built from inception for automation compatibility, modularity, and compliance. The Build phase is structured into seven sub-processes (Figure 9), supporting iteration and parallelization, and is tightly integrated with Design to ensure seamless translation of specifications into robust operational environments.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is also implicated, due to their technical activities with 'data preparation techniques,' system configuration, 'data validation,' and support of studies/projects involving data analysis and processing. As automation is prioritized for assembling and configuring production environments, their work will focus on QA, troubleshooting exceptions, and overseeing the real-time integration and deployment of automated components and data flows.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process describes the activities to reuse existing components or build new components needed for the Process and Analyse phases, as designed in the Design phase. Services (re-)used may include dashboard functions and features, information services, transformation functions, geospatial data services, workflow management tools, respondent and metadata management services.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process describes the activities to reuse existing components or build new, automation-ready components needed for the Process and Analyse phases. All components—whether dashboard modules, transformation functions, geospatial and information services, or workflow management tools—must be designed for modularity, AI/ML-driven orchestration, and seamless integration into digital, event-driven workflows. Automated self-testing, monitoring, and dynamic integration APIs are core features, enabling real-time responsiveness and automated exchange of data and instructions. Human roles focus on oversight, quality assurance, exception management, and iterative modernization of core analytic assets. The process ensures that the full analytics and processing stack evolves toward touchless, scalable, and intelligent operational pipelines.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: GSBPM updates require all components to be 'built or retrofitted for automation, event-driven orchestration, and plug-and-play integration.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' is responsible for supporting 'data preparation techniques,' 'organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies,' and participates in teams for 'data management, research and analysis.' They will need to validate, configure, and ensure technical interoperability of AI/automation-ready analytical and processing modules, testing outputs and troubleshooting integration issues.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Configure workflows
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process configures the workflows, systems and transformations used within the business processes, from data collection through to dissemination. In this sub-process, the workflows are configured based on the design created in sub-process 2.6 (Design production systems and workflows). This could include modifying a standardised workflow for a specific purpose, assembling the workflows for the different phases together (possibly with a workflow/business process management system) and configuring systems accordingly.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process configures the workflows, systems, and transformations used within all business processes—from data collection through to dissemination—to form modular, automation-ready data pipelines. Workflows are assembled, customized, and deployed using digital workflow or business process management platforms, with extensive AI/automation support for orchestration, process monitoring, and autonomous task triggering. These workflows enable seamless, hands-free movement of data and outputs between business process stages, allowing real-time responsiveness and minimizing the need for manual intervention. Human involvement is limited to oversight, rapid workflow adaptation where unique business needs arise, and exception escalation that cannot be managed automatically.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' also plays a part by testing, validating, and advising on digital workflow configuration to support seamless transitions throughout the statistical pipeline. Their technical familiarity with data and process management translates into assisting pipeline monitoring, identifying inefficiencies, and ensuring workflows are correctly parameterized for automation and rapid response.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Create frame and select sample
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of the collection, as specified in sub-process 2.4 (Design frame and sample). It also includes the coordination of samples between instances of the same business process (e.g. to manage overlap or rotation), and between different processes using a common frame or register (e.g. to manage overlap or to spread response burden). Quality assurance and approval of the frame and the selected sample are also undertaken in this sub-process, though maintenance of underlying registers, from which frames for several statistical business processes are drawn, is treated as a separate activity. The sampling aspect of this sub-process is often not relevant for processes based entirely on the use of preexisting sources (e.g. administrative sources and other non-survey sources) as such processes generally create frames from the available data and then follow a census approach. Variables from administrative and other non-statistical sources of data can be used as auxiliary variables in the construction of sampling design.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of the collection, as specified in sub-process 2.4 (Design frame and sample). Automated and AI/LLM-driven technologies are employed to perform record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization across administrative, alternative, and legacy data sources, ensuring the sampling frame is accurate, comprehensive, and consistent. These tools facilitate quality assurance and enhance sample design, especially when coordinating samples between concurrent or overlapping statistical processes. Human experts review, refine, and sign off on the final sampling frame and sample selection, focusing attention on resolving any exceptions or ambiguities surfaced by automated systems.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The GSBPM update requires use of AI/LLM tools for 'record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization across administrative, alternative, and legacy data sources,' improving frame quality. The 'Junior Data Analyst'—with responsibilities for 'data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin'—will primarily validate, QA, and interpret automated frame construction outputs. They will address edge cases, support harmonization efforts, and oversee the integrity of sampling frames generated or enhanced by automation.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Process
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase describes the processing of input data and their preparation for analysis. It is made up of sub-processes that integrate, classify, check, clean, and transform input data, so that they can be analysed and disseminated as statistical outputs. For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. The sub-processes in this phase can apply to data from both statistical and non-statistical sources (with the possible exception of sub-process 5.6 (Calculate weights), which is usually specific to survey data). Some variables could be processed prior to others if they are required for data integration (e.g., geospatial variables if used for that purpose). The Process and Analyse phases can be iterative and parallel. Analysis can reveal a broader understanding of the data, which might make it apparent that additional processing is needed. Sometimes the estimates being processed might be already published aggregates (undertaken according to a Revision Policy). Activities within the Process and Analyse phases may also commence before the Collect phase is completed. This enables the compilation of provisional results where timeliness is an important concern for users, and increases the time available for analysis. The Process phase is broken down into eight sub-processes (Figure 11), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase describes the processing of input data and their preparation for analysis, using modular, version-controlled, automation- and AI/ML-enabled digital workflows. Every sub-process—integrate, classify, check, clean, and transform input data—is configured for event-driven orchestration, reproducibility, and end-to-end automation wherever feasible, ensuring high speed, quality, and consistency. Routine manipulation, error-checking, cleaning, imputation, and integration are handled by AI-enabled modules, with 50% or more of manual interventions eliminated. All processing operations produce full audit trails and documentation for traceability, enabling rapid adjustment and continuous process improvement. Analysts and staff focus on process oversight, exception handling, and innovation, while ensuring all processed outputs are standardized, metadata-rich, and downstream-ready for analysis and dissemination. The Process phase is broken down into eight sub-processes (Figure 11), which may run sequentially, in parallel, or iteratively, as determined by automated orchestration and analytic requirements.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The GSBPM update requires all processing activities—integrating, classifying, transforming, checking, cleaning—to be 'handled via modular, version-controlled, automation-ready digital pipelines, with AI/ML enabling scalable, event-driven, and reproducible execution for each sub-process.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' (‘conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin’) will need to shift from manual execution to oversight, QA, and process innovation for AI/automation-driven pipelines. They focus on configuration, review of exception reports, and iterative improvement of automated processing.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Integrate data
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process integrates data from one or more sources. It is where the results of subprocesses in the Collect phase are combined. The input data can be from a mixture of external or internal sources, and a variety of collection instruments, including extracts of administrative and other non-statistical data sources. Administrative data or other non-statistical sources of data can substitute for all or some of the variables directly collected from a survey. This sub-process also includes harmonising or creating new figures that agree between sources of data. The result is a consolidated set of data.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process integrates data from one or more sources using automated, modular, and AI/LLM-powered pipelines. Record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization are conducted with machine learning and automation as the core methods, minimizing manual intervention. Integration pipelines are event-driven, version-controlled, and produce full audit trails for traceability and continuous improvement. Human experts intervene only to review targeted anomalies, exceptions, and complex analytic challenges, ensuring the integrated dataset is accurate, comprehensive, and ready for further analysis.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The update calls for 'automated, AI/LLM-powered routines for record linking, harmonization, and consolidation of disparate datasets.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' is already experienced in 'data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation.' Now, they supervise, validate, and QA the automated integration outputs, perform expert review of flagged discrepancies or exceptions, and optimize pipelines to achieve reliable consolidated datasets.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Classify and code
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process classifies and codes the input data. For example, automatic (or clerical) coding routines may assign numeric codes to text responses according to a pre-determined statistical classification to facilitate data capture and processing. Some questions have coded response categories on the questionnaires or administrative source of data, others are coded after collection using an automated process (which may apply machine learning or artificial intelligence techniques) or an interactive, manual process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process classifies and codes input data using modular, automated, and AI/ML-powered pipelines that leverage SDMX and other international standards. Text descriptions and response data are classified and coded primarily by LLM/AI models, which assign pre-determined statistical, geospatial, or industry codes with minimal manual handling. The workflow is event-driven, digitally logged, subject to automated QA/review, and fully auditable. Manual intervention is reserved for new or ambiguous cases, or as last-resort exception handling with domain-expert validation. This approach maximizes accuracy, speed, traceability, and scalability for coding/classification at all process scales.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Standardization (e.g., SDMX), event-driven AI/automation, and LLM-powered classification/coding (e.g., NAICS codes) become the default. The 'Junior Data Analyst' role—whose duties include 'data preparation,' 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation'—now requires skills for configuring, validating, and troubleshooting automated classification/coding flows, reviewing outputs, and escalating ambiguous cases for further judgment.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Review and validate
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process examines data to identify potential problems, errors and discrepancies such as outliers, item non-response, miscoding and duplicate records. It can also be referred to as input data validation. It may be run iteratively, validating data against pre-defined edit rules, usually in a set order. It may flag data for automatic or manual inspection or editing. Reviewing and validating can apply to data from any type of source, before and after integration, as well as imputed data from sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute). Whilst validation is treated as part of the Process phase, in practice, some elements of validation may occur alongside collection activities, particularly for approaches such as computer assisted collection. Whilst this sub-process is concerned with detection and localisation of actual or potential errors, any correction activities that actually change the data is done in sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute).
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process examines and validates data using modular, automated digital tools and AI/LLM-enabled validation routines. ML and LLMs flag missing data, inconsistencies, outliers, and errors, routing only ambiguous, complex, or systemic anomalies to human experts for further investigation and correction. All validation is digitally orchestrated with complete audit logging, reproducibility, and ongoing version control. This approach ensures rapid, scalable, and transparent validation with minimal manual intervention, allowing for continuous adjustment and quality improvement.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Routine validation and error/outlier/anomaly detection is automated (AI/LLM), while complex or ambiguous cases go to humans. The 'Junior Data Analyst', tasked with 'ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards...,' will now concentrate on reviewing automated validation reports, responding to escalations from digital pipelines, and suggesting edits or QA rule improvements to continually sharpen automated routines.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Edit and impute
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: Where data are considered incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated, new values may be inserted, or erroneous data may be removed in this sub-process. The terms editing and imputation cover a variety of methods to do this, often using a rule-based approach. Specific steps typically include: Determining whether to add or change data; Selecting the method to be used; Adding/changing data values; Writing the new data values back to the data set, and flagging them as changed; Producing metadata on the editing and imputation process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: Where data are considered incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated, edits and imputations are made through automated, modular, and AI/LLM-powered digital pipelines. LLMs and ML modules suggest and apply replacements or corrections as standard, tracking all actions and metadata in a comprehensive audit trail. Human analysts intervene only for novel, complex, or systemic data problems, and for reviewing and signing off automated edits where required. This ensures fast, accurate, and transparent correction of data with minimal manual processing.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: AI/LLM-driven imputation and edit routines are now standard. The 'Junior Data Analyst'—responsible for data cleansing and transformation—reviews AI-suggested edits, ensures proper logging, investigates cases not resolved by automation, and audits the integrity of metadata on the edit/impute process.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Derive new variables and units
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process derives data for variables and units that are not explicitly provided in the collection, but are needed to deliver the required outputs. It derives new variables by applying arithmetic formulae to one or more of the variables that are already present in the dataset, or applying different model assumptions. This activity may need to be iterative, as some derived variables may themselves be based on other derived variables. It is therefore important to ensure that variables are derived in the correct order. New units may be derived by aggregating or splitting data for collection units, or by various other estimation methods. Examples include deriving households where the collection units are persons or enterprises where the collection units are legal units.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process derives data for variables and units needed to deliver required outputs using modular, automation- and AI-powered methods. Digital pipelines apply arithmetic and formula-based logic, iterating as needed and recording all derivations and transformations with a traceable audit trail. Manual intervention is reserved for rare, non-standard or complex derivations beyond automation, with staff focusing on validation and insight for exceptions. This structure maximizes efficiency, reproducibility, and transparency in all variable/unit derivation steps.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Variable/unit derivations are now 'modular, automation-ready, and AI-powered.' The 'Junior Data Analyst'—with skills in 'modeling, summarization, reporting'—focuses on validating, reviewing, and fine-tuning AI-derived new variables, as well as checking the audit trail and ensuring all derivations conform to expected logic and implementation.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Calculate weights
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process creates weights for unit data records according to the methodology developed in sub-process 2.5 (Design processing and analysis). For example, weights can be used to 'gross-up' data to make them representative of the target population (e.g. for sample surveys or extracts of scanner data), or to adjust for non-response in total enumerations. In other situations, variables may need weighting for normalisation purposes. It may also include weight correction for benchmarking indicators (e.g. known population totals).
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process creates weights for unit data records through modular, event-driven automated algorithms, according to methodologies determined in phase 2.5. All steps and formulae, including adjustments for non-response or benchmarking, are handled digitally and recorded in procedural audit logs. Staff intervene when innovative methods, unexpected results, or diagnostic reviews are needed; otherwise, the process runs hands-free, ensuring speed, precision, and traceability in weight calculation.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Weight calculation is now performed by 'modular, event-driven automated algorithms,' with staff role limited to review of diagnostics, exceptions and innovative methods. The 'Junior Data Analyst' will QA weights, manage exceptions, and validate automated chain logs against established methodology and expected results.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Calculate aggregates
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process creates aggregate data and population totals from microdata or lower-level aggregates. It includes summing data for records sharing certain characteristics (e.g. aggregation of data by demographic or geographic classifications), determining measures of average and dispersion, and applying weights from sub-process 5.6 (Calculate weights) to derive appropriate totals. In the case of statistical outputs which use sample surveys, sampling errors corresponding to relevant aggregates may also be calculated in this sub-process.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process creates aggregate data and population totals using modular, digital automation pipelines, generating all statistical summaries, weights, and dispersion measures hands-free. Event-driven algorithms apply the full range of aggregations, error calculations, and summary statistic logic, recording all processes in comprehensive audit logs for traceability and QA. Human expert action is required only for advanced analytic extensions or for reviewing flagged anomalies or exceptions in automated results.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: Aggregations, summary statistics, and error calculations are conducted in 'modular, automated pipelines.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' ensures the reproducibility and integrity of aggregation outputs, reviews audit trails, and supervises exceptions or advanced analyses beyond automated scope.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Finalise data files
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process brings together the results of the other sub-processes in this phase in a data set (either micro- or macro-data), which is used as the input to the Analyse phase. Sometimes, this may be an intermediate rather than a final data set, particularly for business processes where there are strong time pressures, and a requirement to produce both preliminary and final estimates.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This sub-process brings together and finalizes the results of all previous sub-processes in the phase, producing data files (micro- or macro-level) in fully standardized, open, and machine-actionable formats by default. All datasets and supporting documentation are versioned, digitally logged, and immediately available for reproducible handoff to subsequent analysis or dissemination phases. Technical staff ensure compliance with standards and continuous skills development, and all processes are supported by automated documentation and audit trails, supporting immediate traceability, interoperability, and readiness for deployment across business domains.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' must support documentation and QA of new automated outputs, enforce standards, validate technical hand-off, and conduct audits or troubleshooting where needed. Their role requires technical proficiency and validation mindset to guarantee all outputs meet evolving standards for machine/human consumption.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Specify needs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options and preparing a business case, which may weigh the benefits of addressing these needs against expected costs, risks and other requirements, considering the public good arising from meeting those needs and the implications for respondents, users and other stakeholders. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.
implicated phases and sub-processes.updated description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options, and preparing a business case. In the modernized statistical environment, these activities are increasingly supported by automated and AI-powered processes—ranging from the synthesis and structuring of stakeholder inputs, through the analysis of options, to the automated drafting of business case materials. Routine and repetitive aspects of needs identification, consultation, and documentation are minimized for manual intervention, enabling staff to focus on higher-value tasks: interpreting context, establishing priorities, and making strategic decisions that cannot be automated. The phase thus leverages end-to-end process automation and AI wherever possible, supporting greater efficiency, responsiveness, and quality at the earliest stage of the statistical business process. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.
implicated phases and sub-processes.justification: The 'Junior Evaluation Officer' role is directly implicated because the work-description states they 'conduct literature and data research, identify, gather, analyze and synthesize quantitative and qualitative data,' and 'provide input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions.' With automation handling more routine synthesis, this officer will need to shift toward high-value interpretation and oversight of AI-supported outputs: 'The incumbent is required to communicate with clients in the data acquisition process; prepare statistical and narrative summaries for review...' They will be more involved in validating AI summaries, contextualizing input data, and making recommendations based on AI-driven drafts.

implicated phases and sub-processes.title: Identify needs
implicated phases and sub-processes.original description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics.
